skill.name: writing-config-files
skill.description: Use this skill when you need to write configuration files in `src/config` for the Next.js app
skill.summary: Use this skill when you need to write configuration files in `src/config` for the Next.js app
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code backticks around src/config. SKILL.md contains prompt guidance only, with no command execution, network access, or prompt injection evidence.

static_findings.snippet: description: Use this skill when you need to write configuration files in `src/config` for the Next.
- Follow the rules below to write config files for the Next.js app in `src/config`:

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 3 uses Markdown inline code to name the src/config directory. There is no shell, Ruby, or executable context.
Line 8 uses Markdown inline code to describe the target folder. The backticks are formatting only and do not invoke commands.

content.value_statement: Next.js config folders can become hard to maintain when many settings live together. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create small modular files.
actual_capabilities: Guides configuration files to live under src/config.
Encourages one config function or variable per file.
Limits each config file to 50 lines.
Promotes modular file separation when possible.
Applies simple structure rules for Next.js configuration work.
limitations: Does not define project-specific config names or schemas.
Does not validate generated code against a running Next.js app.
Does not include scripts, tests, or automated file generation.
Assumes the project already uses a src/config directory.

use_cases.title: Organize App Settings
use_cases.description: Create separate config files for settings that should not share one large module.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Output
use_cases.description: Give AI assistants clear rules for config file size, location, and structure.

use_cases.title: Refactor Config Sprawl
use_cases.description: Split broad config modules into smaller files with one exported concept per file.

prompt_templates.title: Create One Config
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single setting group.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a small Next.js config file under src/config for feature flags. Keep it modular and under 50 lines.

prompt_templates.title: Split Related Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for multiple related config areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create config files for analytics and navigation settings. Put each function or variable in its own src/config file.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Config
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to reorganize a large config module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this large config module and suggest how to split it into src/config files with one export per file.

prompt_templates.title: Design Config Layout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a maintainable folder plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a src/config structure for a growing Next.js app. Separate concerns, keep files short, and explain each file purpose.

output_examples.input: Create feature flag configuration for a Next.js app.
output_examples.output: A short feature flag config file placed in src/config, with one exported value and clear naming.

output_examples.input: Split analytics and navigation settings into separate config files.
output: One analytics config file with only analytics settings.
One navigation config file with only navigation settings.
Each file stays below the requested size limit.

output_examples.input: Refactor a large config module into smaller files.
output_examples.output: A proposed file split that separates each config function or variable into its own src/config file.

best_practices: Keep each config file focused on one exported concept.
Use clear file names that describe the config purpose.
Split config files before they exceed the 50 line limit.
anti_patterns: Do not place unrelated settings in one large config file.
Do not create config files outside src/config without a project reason.
Do not mix multiple config functions or variables in one file.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create small configuration files for a Next.js app under src/config.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt guidance and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Can it validate my config values?
faq.answer: No. It guides structure, but project validation must come from your app and tests.

faq.question: Why limit files to 50 lines?
faq.answer: The limit encourages smaller files that are easier to review, reuse, and maintain.

faq.question: Can it handle several config areas?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages splitting separate concerns into separate src/config files.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
